candidate.title: Ribose-seq
candidate.scope: The Illumina Ribose-seq schematic row, from genomic DNA bearing embedded ribonucleotides through the DNA-for-sequencing endpoint. The route is clarified using Koh et al., Nature Methods 12, 251–257 (2015), PMID 25622106, DOI 10.1038/nmeth.3259, with full-text content inspected. Adjacent HydEn-seq, G4-seq, partial Digenome-seq material and the right-hand base-structure legend are not alternative targets of this assigned row. AtRNL self-ligation is a component of Ribose-seq, not a separate target method. This describes the shown architecture rather than all experimental implementations.

operations.description: Remove the residual 2′-phosphate at the capture-circle ligation junction, then PCR-amplify the adaptor-associated captured DNA to produce the DNA-for-sequencing endpoint. The drawing places a circular icon at this combined caption and a linear product at the endpoint.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper identifies 2′-phosphotransferase Tpt1 for junction-phosphate removal before PCR; the schematic groups removal and PCR in one block.

UMI-bearing adaptors in that implementation permit PCR-copy discrimination; 3′-phosphate cleavage products are not captured by AtRNL, and only the 5′-most rNMP in a consecutive tract is represented.
